FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.lock: A per-CommercialAccount advisory lock is taken before any state read that a write depends on, mirroring the per-organization lock of stella_0016 that lib/stella/quota.ts records as the fix for the read-then-write race.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.lock_ordering: Where both an account lock and an organization lock are needed, the ACCOUNT lock is taken FIRST, always. A fixed global order is what makes deadlock structurally impossible rather than rare.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.two_shapes_not_one: There are TWO transaction shapes, and which one applies is determined by the transition, not by the caller.
transaction_boundaries: SHAPE A - SPLIT (the default, for suspension, reactivation and plan re-evaluation). T1 state transaction: ledger completion + commercial state write + subscription-fact write + re-evaluation request row + state audit row. T2 entitlement transaction: grant closures and openings + entitlement audit rows + legacy projection write; separate, idempotent by the request's cause_identity.

SHAPE B - ATOMIC (CANCELLATION ONLY). TC: ledger completion + commercial state write + subscription-identity clearing + PLAN grant closures + BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT replacements + state audit row + per-grant entitlement audit rows. ONE transaction, commit together or roll back together. No request row is emitted because nothing is deferred.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.why_shape_A_is_split: STRIPE_BOUNDARY.downstream_reaction prohibits the WEBHOOK from one transaction that both records a subscription and moves a quota. The split is not an optimisation; it is that boundary.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.why_shape_B_is_atomic: OD-6 requires the three conjuncts of cancellation to happen together (MC-5). It does not breach the webhook prohibition because the webhook does not perform it - a distinct governed capability does (CANCELLATION.performed_by), and that capability is authorized for the CLOSING direction only, so the creation risk the prohibition exists to stop is absent by construction.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.the_window_in_shape_A: Closed by EC-4's conjunctive gate, evaluated from commercial_status at enforcement time. For SUSPENDED the gate is BLOCKED, so T1 having committed is sufficient and the window fails CLOSED. The gate is NOT sufficient for cancellation, whose target gate is pass-through - which is why cancellation is Shape B.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.there_is_no_window_in_shape_B: TC either committed, in which case the state is BOOTSTRAP and the grants are closed, or it did not, in which case nothing changed. A torn cancellation is not a state the database can represent.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.T2_failure: If T2 fails, the request row stays unconsumed and is retried. The gate keeps a SUSPENDED account closed meanwhile. Repeated failure ESCALATES. An unconsumed obligation additionally REFUSES any transition into ACTIVE_STRIPE or ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE with cause pending_closure_obligation - see CANCELLATION.INV_STALE_GRANT, which is what stops a reactivation from resuming on condemned grants.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.TC_failure: The whole cancellation rolls back. The account keeps its pre-cancellation state, its subscription identity and its live grants - the pre-transition truth, not a remnant. The ledger row remains unfinished, the handler answers 503, and Stripe redelivers. Repeated failure ESCALATES.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.T1_failure: The ledger row remains 'processing' and the handler answers 503, inviting redelivery. stripe_fail_event marks it failed from the handler's catch block AFTER the apply has raised and rolled back - the existing separation (db/prepared/stella_0008_stripe_webhook_identity.sql:43-46, 854-885) that exists precisely because an UPDATE followed by a RAISE in one transaction rolls its own bookkeeping back. Preserved.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.concurrent_events_same_account: Serialized by the advisory lock. The loser re-reads state inside its own lock hold and then evaluates ORD-3 and ORD-4 against the winner's committed result, which is why ORD-6 requires the guard to be inside the lock.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.concurrent_first_bindings: Serialized by the lock; the loser observes a non-NULL stripe_customer_id and returns it as a NO-OP. Should the lock ever be bypassed, UNIQUE(stripe_customer_id) refuses the second write. Should the API call itself be duplicated, the Stripe idempotency key keyed on commercial_account_id returns the same customer. Three independent bounds.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.partial_multi_org_application: An account governing N Organizations applies its entitlement effect N times. In Shape A, T2 is atomic across all N: a state change that lands for some Organizations and not others is PROHIBITED; if N is large enough that one transaction is impractical, the request row is split per Organization with per-Organization idempotency, and EC-4's gate keeps every not-yet-applied Organization correct in the meantime. In Shape B, TC is atomic across all N BY DEFINITION - splitting it would reintroduce exactly the torn cancellation OD-6 forbids. An account whose N makes one cancellation transaction impractical is an ESCALATION, not a licence to split.
FAILURE_AND_CONCURRENCY.escalation_means: STOP and surface. An escalating condition (ambiguous_order, subscription_conflict, manual_basis_conflict, binding collision, repeated T2 failure, repeated TC failure, repeated pending_closure_obligation) is never auto-resolved, never guessed, and never silently retried into a different outcome. Fail closed where authority is ambiguous.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: Cancellation has a PRE-transition window: between the webhook recording the observed cancellation and the cancellation capability committing, the tenant still holds live capacity.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: BOUNDED RESIDUAL, accepted and stated. In this window the commercial state and the grants AGREE with each other and with the last applied truth - the account still reads ACTIVE_STRIPE with live grants, which is simply the state before the transition is applied. It is categorically unlike R1's window, in which state said BOOTSTRAP while PLAN grants stayed live and no gate closed them. Eliminating this window entirely would require the webhook itself to perform the entitlement write, which STRIPE_BOUNDARY.webhook_prohibitions forbids outright. The tradeoff is therefore forced, not chosen, and the safe side of it is the one taken.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: SUSPENSION remains Shape A (split), so an unconsumed closure obligation can coexist with a SUSPENDED account, and a reactivation arriving in that window must not resume on condemned grants.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Resolved by CANCELLATION.INV_STALE_GRANT, which makes 'no unconsumed closure obligation' a PRECONDITION of every transition into ACTIVE_STRIPE and ACTIVE_WITHOUT_STRIPE, refusing with pending_closure_obligation. Recorded as a finding rather than buried in the invariant because it is the one place where Shape A's asynchrony reaches a state OTHER than the one it was gating.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The cancellation capability is the only identity authorized to write commercial_accounts and entitlement_grants in one transaction.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Concentration of privilege, deliberate and bounded. The whole safety argument is the CLOSING-DIRECTION-ONLY restriction, which must be an asserted postcondition on the verb (it cannot open a PLAN grant), not a convention. Recorded so the D-8 reviewer treats that assertion as the gate rather than as documentation.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: D-8's cancellation capability role will need the same membership boundary as uellix_cap_commercial, and this authority freezes that boundary only for uellix_cap_commercial.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: PROPAGATION OBLIGATION, recorded not resolved. The membership argument is general: ANY policy written TO a capability role is only as strong as the set of roles that can inherit it. D-8's node MUST carry its own ZERO ROLE MEMBERS postcondition with the same pg_auth_members proof; this authority does not pre-author D-8's postconditions because it does not allocate D-8. Recorded so the omission is visible rather than inherited by silence.

R3.blocker_membership_boundary: R2 froze uellix_cap_commercial's attributes but never bounded WHO MAY INHERIT IT. A PostgreSQL policy written TO a role applies through role membership, so a foreign login granted membership would inherit P1's permissive admission and combine it with a caller-controlled app.commercial_account_id. The row bound answers WHICH ROW, never WHO MAY ACTIVATE THE ROLE. ZERO ROLE MEMBERS is now an asserted postcondition with a pg_auth_members catalogue proof keyed on roleid, named in RLS.decision.role, argued in RLS.decision.membership_boundary_is_a_security_boundary_of_the_policy_pair, and carried into FUTURE_DDL.D-6 as PC-3.
R3.provenance_correction: R1 and R2 cited stella_0008:938 as the CAPABILITY-role precedent in four places. Re-measured at AS_OF: :938-941 asserts the forbidden attributes for uellix_stripe, the LOGIN role; the capability-role precedent is :948-950 (NOLOGIN) and :951-956 (zero members). All four sites corrected, and the places where this authority requires MORE than the precedent now say so instead of borrowing authority they do not have.
R3.NB-1_precision: R2's rationale claimed USING alone would let an admitted row be rewritten outside the bound. FALSE - PostgreSQL reuses USING as WITH CHECK when WITH CHECK is absent. The claim is withdrawn and replaced with the real reasons both clauses are written (explicitness, auditability via pg_policies.with_check, drift resistance). The DDL design is UNCHANGED: both clauses remain mandatory.
